newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks fall 2.3 pct, sixth weakest close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks fall 2.3 pct, sixth weakest close.

text.p: Toronto stocks closed down 2.3 percent on Wednesday, the sixth biggest daily decline for Canada's largest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index sank 138.17 points to finish at 5781.69 in heavy turnover of 106.4 million shares worth C$1.79 billion.

Declining stocks overwhelmed advancers 753 to 280, with 251 issues unchanged. Wednesday's free fall wiped out the Toronto market's gains over the past two sessions. Analysts attributed the selloff to profit taking by foreign investors, slumping oil prices and weakness in U.S. markets.
"Japanese investors were selling North American bonds and stocks to repatriate some of the money back to the Japanese market," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities.
The decline in Canadian bonds and currency began overnight and spilled over into stocks Wednesday at the open.

Katzin said some investors were concerned that certain sectors were overvalued since the TSE had gained almost 25 percent this year. All 14 sub-groups finished lower, led by a 415 point decline in golds. Energy stocks fell 175 points due to sharply weaker oil prices.

* Among golds, Barrick Gold Corp dropped 2.75 to 38.50, while Placer Dome Inc lost 1.20 to close at 30.80. Trading in Bre-X Minerals Ltd was halted ahead of an announcement from the company expected on Thursday. Bre-X and Barrick have been in joint venture talks over the Busang gold discovery.
* Potash Corp of Saskatchewan Inc led net losers, falling 5.35 to 112.20. Investment broker Merrill Lynch cut its near-term rating on Potash Corp to neutral on Wednesday.
* Renaissance Energy was the weakest oil issue, down 2.15 to 45.30.
